messages:
maria: quick sync — i've been digging into the service auth cleanup and we need a concrete checklist for migrating from flat api-keys to scoped keys (project/org + intent).
alex: +1. can you sketch the high-level flow? i worry about live traffic and third-party integrations.
sam: two quick constraints: 1) we can't break existing webhook consumers, 2) operator scripts rely on unscoped keys in a few places.
maria: agreed. proposed flow: 1) add scoped-key support in auth service (dual-accept mode), 2) telemetry to tag usage by key-type, 3) opt-in create-scoped-keys UI + cli, 4) gradual enforcement via canary route, 5) enforce-only after 90 days and bulk-migrate remaining keys.
jen: how does dual-accept work? do we accept both header formats? example?
maria: yes — server accepts old header: `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` and new header: `Authorization: ApiKey scope=project:proj-123;intent=ingest;<key>` — nothing fancy in v1, just a prefixed kv blob. auth service extracts scope/intent if present.
leo: prefer explicit k=v syntax, maybe `Authorization: ApiKey key=<key> scope=project:proj-123` so parsers are deterministic. also we should avoid parsing issues with semicolons.
alex: +1 on deterministic parsing. also we should include a token `kid` in the payload so we can rotate without invalidating identifiers: `Authorization: ApiKey key=<kid>:<sig> scope=...`
jen: operationally, what's our recommended fallback for services that can't immediately support the new header? do we allow a proxy shim?
maria: yes — recommended pattern: 1) deploy auth-side dual-accept, 2) deploy a lightweight gateway shim that rewrites old header to new keyed form for legacy services, 3) add `x-deprecation-warning` responses when legacy key used in canary routes.
sam: what about RBAC mapping? scoped keys should map to least-privilege role set. do we change role model?
maria: keep RBAC surface stable — scoped keys map to existing role ids via a translation table. new keys carry `intent` which we use to auto-select a role if none explicitly bound. example mapping: `intent:ingest -> role:ingest-writer`
leo: can we publish a sample policy json for operators to review?
maria: sure, rough example below:
```json
{
  "key_id": "kid-123",
  "scope": "project:proj-123",
  "intent": "ingest",
  "roles": ["ingest-writer"],
  "created_by": "svc-deployer",
  "ttl": 2592000
}
```
alex: nice. next: telemetry. we need to tag every auth check with `auth_key_type={legacy|scoped}` and `migration_stage={dual|canary|enforce}` so we can query SLO impact.
jen: and add audit events for any shim rewrite so we can later list integrations that still need upgrades.
sam: migration window and deprecation timeline? 90 days seems okay but we should make it configurable per org. some customers will need longer.
maria: propose default 90d, but enterprise accounts can request a 180d extension. we'll add an admin flag `auth.migration_window_override`.
leo: rollout plan bullets?
maria: short checklist for the RFC doc we can attach to deploy tickets: - implement parsing/stable schema for scoped header in auth service (dual-accept) - add `kid` support + local rotation tooling - gateway shim + shim audit logs - UI/CLI to create scoped keys and bulk-migration tool - telemetry labels and dashboards - canary routing: enable strict-scoped rules for 5% traffic for 2 weeks - deprecation warning header when legacy key used in canary - enforcement cutoff + bulk rotate remaining keys - customer communications + migration playbook
alex: can we make the canary rule per-route instead of global? some routes are more sensitive.
maria: yes — route-scoped canaries. add a `route_migration_policy` in the rollout.
jen: who wants to own the bulk-migration tool? sounds like platform-tools + security pair.
sam: i'll volunteer to shepherd the tool and help with operator scripts.
leo: i'll take the canary routing and telemetry dashboards.
alex: i'll draft the RFC with the checklist and rough endpoint contracts.
